name: stream_kpa_check
description: Check key and nonce hypotheses against a family of encrypted files by the first bytes each file should have, and say exactly what was tried. RULES for an encrypted-file family (they are in every answer too): (1) measure what the encryptor added before hunting a key: a member against a same-name plaintext twin, the members against each other (encrypted_survey reports the overhead, the smallest member and whether the tails are unique per file); (2) read the encryption routine to the key's LAST use: where is the per-file key written? A constant-size trailer or header that is unique per file is where per-file key material is usually kept, often masked by a constant: test it (stream_kpa_check) before hunting memory; (3) one known (file, key) pair verifies any footer hypothesis; (4) a scan that finds nothing is a negative only after its planted control passed, and only for the shapes it lists. The chain, with no code to write: cipher_state_scan on a process dump (key and nonce candidates to a values file) -> stream_kpa_check on the encrypted files with that values file as key and nonce source (verdict per file, and the recipe) -> family_decrypt with the recipe file (every member, a receipt each). Inputs: the members (files, or dir with glob and recursive); the expected first bytes by the type in each member's name (photo.png.locked is a png; built in: png, jpg, gif, bmp, tif, psd, webp, pdf, rtf, zip/docx/xlsx/pptx/odt/jar/apk, doc/xls/ppt/msg, mp4/m4a/m4v/3gp/heic/mov (ftyp at offset 4), avi/wav (RIFF), mkv, flac, ogg, wmv, sqlite, 7z, rar, gz, xz, bz2, exe/dll, elf, lnk, evtx, pst, pcap, vhdx, vmdk; more with `magics`), and, when a same-name plaintext twin lies beside a member (the name without its last extension), the twin's first 64 bytes; and SOURCES for the key and for the nonce. A source is an object with exactly one of: {"hex": "..."} (a literal; it is recorded with the call, so use it for a constant read from the sample, such as a mask or a nonce, and give a key by reference), {"file": path, "offset": n, "length": n} (bytes of a file: a constant inside the sample, a key file), {"candidates": path} (the values file of cipher_state_scan: every key in it, or every nonce in each layout), or {"slice": "head" or "tail", "length": n, "skip": n, "xor": {a hex or file source of the same length}} (bytes of each member itself: its first or last n bytes after skipping `skip`, optionally XORed with a constant). Every key and nonce the sources yield is tried on every member that has a crib, with each cipher in `ciphers` (chacha20-ietf: 12-byte nonce and 32-bit counter; chacha20-original: 8-byte nonce and 64-bit counter; salsa20: 8-byte nonce, 20 rounds; aes-ctr: a 16-byte nonce is the first counter block, a 12-byte one is followed by a 32-bit big-endian counter, an 8-byte one by a 64-bit one; rc4; xor with a repeating key) at each counter in `counters` (default 0 and 1). A cipher for which the sources yield no key or no nonce of a length it takes makes no trial: tried.trials_by_cipher counts the trials the sources gave each cipher and not_tried names the ciphers that had none; a member on which no trial at all could be made has the verdict not_tried, never no_match, and the answer is partial. A candidates file that holds no key is refused with what it held (its rows, how many were not usable). A candidates file is read one line at a time, under the clock, and parsed once per role however many sources name it (the same file by device and inode: the later ones say same_file_as); it is refused unread above 64 MiB and refused at its 20,001st non-empty line (cipher_state_scan writes 5000 rows at most), a line longer than 64 KiB is counted as not usable without being parsed, at most 8 layouts of a row give a nonce, a key longer than 256 bytes or a nonce of a length no cipher takes (not 8, 12 or 16) is counted and not kept, and the sources of one call may yield at most 40,000 distinct keys and 40,000 distinct nonces (more is refused, before anything is tried). The ciphertext is taken to start at header_bytes (default: what the head slices take); only the first 64 bytes of a member are decrypted, in memory. THE FOOTER HYPOTHESIS IS MADE FOR YOU (`derive`, default true): when a key that is not a slice (a key from a dump, of 256 bytes at most) opens a member, that key XOR the member's own last (or, inside header_bytes, first) bytes at every skip from 0 to 64 is taken as a constant mask, and each such mask is tried on EVERY other member that has a crib and that no key rule explains yet: first with the cipher, nonce source and counter that opened the first member, then with every cipher, nonce and counter of the call. A key that opened several members is paired with the first of them (the longest crib first) for each crib length, and the other pairs are counted (tried.derivation.pairs_not_used, and not_tried): a second member of the same crib length is the hypothesis that the first opening was by chance, which the crib cannot tell apart. At most 65,536 places are listed, made one at a time with the clock read; the others are counted (places_not_listed), and the hypothesis is then stopped by max_places: the answer is partial. No place is given up because some members did not open: a member whose content is not what its name promises never shows its crib and is no evidence against a rule, so the answer for a family does not follow the order of its members' names. A member that the best key rule (one that opens two members or more) does not open keeps the verdict no_match, and its row's note says that its content may not be the type its name says (no crib, then) or that it follows another rule. A mask that opens another member is reported in derived_rules and can become the recipe's key rule; once a key rule explains a member, later masks are not tried on it, and the hypothesis ends when one rule explains every member. These trials count against max_trials and the clock: when either (or the bound on places listed) stops the hypothesis before every place was tried so, the answer is partial, partial_reasons, not_tried and tried.derivation (pairs, pairs_not_used, places, places_not_listed, places_tried_on_every_member, stopped_by: max_trials, max_seconds or max_places) say how far it got, and a no_match row says that it does not cover the hypothesis. At most 64 matching combinations are kept per member (and per member for one derived rule); more are counted (the row's matches_not_kept), and the answer is partial: a crib that short matches by chance, and the rule, the hypothesis and the recipe are made from the kept ones. Output: `outcome` (one_rule_explains_every_member, some_members_explained, no_combination_matched, nothing_to_check, nothing_tried: no member has a verdict, because no trial could be made on a member that has a crib or the clock left every member), one row per member (verdict match, no_match, no_crib, head_is_plaintext, too_small, read_failed or not_tried; the combinations that matched, named by the place of their sources in the call and by finding id; crib_bytes; trials; expected_false_positives = trials times 2^(-8 x crib length), and a crib_note for a crib of 4 bytes or less), the totals, `tried` (ciphers, counters, layouts, each source by kind and length, the bounds) and `not_tried`. A NEGATIVE is bounded: no_combination_matched says none of the listed trials gave the expected first bytes; it never says that no key exists (not tried: other modes and ciphers, other counters, a key derived by a KDF or wrapped by RSA, another slice, an encryption that skips the first block). A match is the expected first bytes under one combination, not an integrity check: a stream cipher has none. `status` is about the check (complete: every member named was opened and every planned trial run, the footer hypothesis included; partial: max_files, max_trials or the clock stopping the footer hypothesis, the clock, a member with no trial, an unreadable file), `outcome` is about what it found. SENSITIVE: no plaintext byte and no key, nonce or mask byte is in the answer, nor whether a mask is all zero (a key kept unmasked): the recipe file says that (key_mask_all_zero). The recipe (the key rule with its mask, the nonce, the cipher per member, header and trailer bytes; a member is named in its assignments by its path below dir, or below the directory the files share, so two members of one name in two directories are two entries; member_suffix is the extension the explained members share, compared in any case and written as most of them write it) holds key material and is written to stream-recipe.json under $OUT only in a job run as secret output (the manifest makes every job of this tool one); outside one the verdicts are given and the recipe is not written, with the reason. A recipe is written when its rule explains every member with a crib, or at least two of them (then family_decrypt marks the others as not confirmed), and when it needs at most 16 combinations of cipher, nonce and counter (what family_decrypt reads; the answer lists 16 and counts the rest). It is written under a temporary name (.stream-recipe.json.part) with the stop signals held, then given its name without replacing a file that is there (stream-recipe.json, else -2, -3 ...); a stop before the answer is printed removes it, and a kill no handler sees leaves the .part file, never a cut recipe. Its trailer_bytes is what the call gave, or at least what the key and nonce slices take from the end: a longer trailer leaves its other bytes at the end of each decrypted file, and encrypted_survey's overhead against a plaintext twin is the measure. Every input is read after the tool's clock is set (it runs from the start of the call), and every loop that reads an input or makes a hypothesis reads the clock. A directory is listed one entry at a time, the clock read every 1024 entries, keeping at most twice the room left under max_files of the names that match and at most 100,000 directories still to list (the others are counted). Memory: the sources' distinct values (at most 40,000 per role, about 1 KB each with their labels), the kept matches, at most 65,536 places with their masks (256 bytes at most each) and a cache of at most 200,000 first keystream blocks; a 64 MiB candidates file of 20,000 rows named 16 times as key and 16 times as nonce source was read in under a second at about 70 MB resident. Bounds: max_files (default 200), max_trials (default 500000, for the sources' trials and the footer hypothesis together; a call whose sources alone would pass it is refused before anything is tried, with the count: when one member alone would pass it, before any member is opened, and otherwise once the members are read; the trials are counted from the lengths of what the sources give, never listed in memory, and made one at a time), max_seconds (default 480, below the manifest's 600; the clock is read every 256 trials, in the footer hypothesis too); a trial costs about 0.1 ms in pure Python; a member whose trials the clock cuts has the verdict not_tried, never a match or a miss. A link is not followed and only regular files are read; one member is open at a time, so a family of thousands needs one descriptor. A stop signal ends it with one JSON answer (status failed, interrupted) and no recipe. Paths and file names are printed as given, whatever their characters (the answer is JSON, which escapes what is not ASCII), a path cut at 1024 characters.

files.description: Paths of the encrypted members (1 to 100000). Give this or dir

dir.description: A directory holding the members; with glob and recursive. Give this or files

glob.description: A pattern on a file's name within dir (default "*"; "*.locked" keeps to the members)

recursive.description: true: also the directories below dir (no link followed). Default false

max_files.description: The most members checked (default 200, at most 5000), in the order of their names; more than this makes the answer partial

key_sources.description: Sources of the key, each tried (required, at most 32; at most 40,000 distinct keys in all; a candidates file of at most 64 MiB and 20,000 lines, read once however often it is named). Examples: [{"candidates": "store/jobs/j000012/out/cipher-state-candidates.jsonl"}] for keys from a dump; [{"slice": "tail", "length": 32}, {"slice": "tail", "length": 32, "xor": {"file": "work/sample.exe", "offset": 91200, "length": 32}}] for a per-file key in a 32-byte trailer, plain or masked by a constant of the sample

nonce_sources.description: Sources of the nonce, each tried (at most 32; rc4 and xor need none). A candidates file yields every state's nonce in each layout (12 bytes IETF, 8 bytes original)

ciphers.description: Ciphers to try: any of "chacha20-ietf", "chacha20-original", "salsa20", "aes-ctr", "rc4", "xor" (default all six)

counters.description: First block numbers to try (default [0, 1]; 1 to 8 numbers)

magics.description: More expected first bytes by extension: {"dwg": "41433130"} or {"iso": {"hex": "4344303031", "offset": 1}} (hex, within the first 64 bytes); an entry replaces a built-in one

header_bytes.description: Bytes at the start of each member that are not ciphertext (default: what the head slices of the sources take, else 0)

trailer_bytes.description: Bytes at the end of each member that are not ciphertext (default: what the tail slices take; the recipe carries it). Give the overhead encrypted_survey measured against a plaintext twin

derive.description: Make the footer hypothesis from a key that opened one member (default true); false tries only the sources as given

max_trials.description: The most trials in all (default 500000, at most 5000000); the sources' trials and the footer hypothesis together. A call whose sources alone would pass it is refused before anything is tried (before any member is opened when one member alone would pass it); a footer hypothesis it stops makes the answer partial

max_seconds.description: The tool's own time limit in seconds (default 480, at most 540; the manifest's timeout is 600)

limit.description: Member rows shown inline (default 200, at most 5000)
